sources.entry: Sloth - Sloth is an macOS application that displays a list of all open files and sockets in use by all running applications on your system.

summary.one_liner: Sloth is a native macOS app that shows all open files, directories, sockets, pipes, and devices used by running processes, built as a GUI on top of the lsof command.
summary.what_it_does: Sloth lists open files, directories, IP sockets, devices, Unix domain sockets, and pipes for all running processes on a Mac. It parses the output of the lsof command-line tool and shows it in a sortable, searchable outline view. Users can filter by name, access mode, volume, type, location, or regular expressions, and sort by process name, file count, type, process ID, user ID, and other fields. It shows IP socket status, protocol, port and version, plus sockets and pipes connected between processes. An inspection window gives detailed macOS and Unix file, socket, and process info, and a contextual menu offers file operations. The app can authenticate in-app to scan with root privileges.
use_cases: find which app has a file open
inspect open network sockets and ports on a Mac
see inter-process pipes and socket connections
troubleshoot files locked by running processes
scan open files with root privileges
browse lsof output without the terminal
how_to_run: Download Sloth 3.6 from the project's download link (macOS 11 or later)
Or install via Homebrew: brew install --cask sloth
To build from source, run from the repository root: make build_unsigned (requires Xcode build tools)
Built products are created in products/
notable: Friendly graphical front end to the lsof command-line tool
Sortable, searchable outline view with regex filtering
Inspection window with detailed Unix and macOS file, socket and process info
In-app authentication to scan with root privileges
caveats: Requires macOS 11 or later for the current version; older macOS versions need version 3.4 (10.13-10.15) or 3.2 (10.9-10.12)
Homebrew install may not be the latest version
Building from source requires Xcode build tools
